answer: A shared network stays trustworthy only when ordinary members can check each other's work. The word nebula points to that checkability: a claim that leaves evidence can be re-examined later, instead of being believed once and forgotten. The word horizon points to the incentive behind it: people keep contributing when honest effort is recognised and shortcuts gain nothing. The word jade brings the two together, because a durable community is built by participants who return, verify, and help the next round run fairly.
